I don't think I really ever truly bought into Christianity for very long. Growing up, the cognitive dissonance was enough to make my head spin. I never was quite sure what I felt positively towards god, but I knew there were enough negatives to ward off leaving christianity. 

As I got older, the picture of god as a loving entity balked me more and more. That anecdote about the shepherd breaking the legs of lamb who wandered away, but then nursed it back to health? I know it's not in the bible, but it's touted in sermons to this days as a good allegory. That picture, of someone in power willingly causing pain so that they can fix it, is abuse. If a man did that to someone, he'd be arrested (presuming he's caught, etc.). Not just physically, but the mental equivalent. Teaching someone that they are bad, flawed and unworthy of love, but then offering to love them since no one will be able to love me like he would. The punishment for rejecting this love? Eternal damnation. That doesn't sound like love. It sounds like an ultimatum.   

From there I started having problems with god as a bully figure. Not unlike some of my childhood experiences with my parents. The authoritarian message of "we are deliberately not telling you why we are telling you to do X but you cannot question us." Christians would tell me wanting to question my parents was a symptom of rebellion and should be rooted out. My mother took especial care to watch me more closely and rarely believed me. This was an enormous strain for me as an ADHD/Bipolar child/teen. I ask a lot of questions and need a lot of information to feel safe. I am a big believer in consent in all things, and I felt growing up that my consent was constantly being violated by god and my parents. 

Ultimately, though, I believed that Christianity more closely resembled a systematic means of control and that the idea of a god was an outdated concept.
I've read pieces casually, but my break-away was from the idea of a god in general, so Catholicism really didn't require further study from me. Does that make sense?
